recipes.name: Pork Chops in Beer
ingredients_raw: 1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle beer

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
In a medium bowl, combine the ketchup, brown sugar and beer. Mix well and pour into a 9x13 inch baking dish. Place the pork chops over this mixture in the dish.
Bake, uncovered, at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 1 hour, or internal pork temperature reaches 145 degrees F (63 degrees C). (Note: Place foil over pork chops if they start to brown too quickly.)

raw_recipe.headline: Pork Chops in Beer
raw_recipe.description: Whip up a pungent mixture of ketchup, beer and brown sugar for a sweet and sassy pork chop bake.

review.reviewBody: I honestly do not understand why this recipe is rating so low!! THE CHOPS were PERFECT!! and super easy too!! I let the chops sit in the sauce for about an hour and a half prior to cooking. This made them super tender!!! I also added in a few 'smashed' cloves of garlic, some pepper, a pinch of cayenne, a dash of dry moustard and a couple dashes of worchestire sauce. Alongside the chops (in the sauce) I also added some largely chopped green and red peppers, and some onions. THEY WERE GREAT and a hit with the family... the beer was the perfect taste... not over powering at all!! LOVED THEM!! I would recommend this one again and again!

i added one large onion sliced, a yellow and a red bellpeper, a stick of celery chopped, two carrots sliced. i put all this over the porckchops in a backing pan. in the sauce i used german beer (i prefar german beer because it is stronger and tastes better) i replaced the ketchup with a hunt's can of petite diced tomatoes. also added two tbsp of crushed garlic (i buy the fresh crushed one in a jar) a bit of large crushed pepper, rosemary, thyme, oregano.(the leafs i used the mccormik gourmet colection, they come in a clear spice jar with a green label and a black cap) i poured the sauce over the chopes and made sure they were all berried under the sauce. also i stabbed the porkschops before putting them into the pan so they will marinate better. i put them in the fridge to marinate for about 24 h+ (made them on sundey morning and cooked them monday afternoon for dinner.) i baked them covered in foil for 50 minutes and then without the foil for another 10. i used some of the liquid to cook some rice as a side dish. me and my husband loved this one. he gave me 9 stars out of 10 so i am pretty sure we will be making this again
Pretty good but next time I'll leave out the brown sugar, dry brine the chops and sear them before braising. I also added onions since that's how my mom used to make these.

I followed the advice of some other reviewers and tweeked the recipe a bit. I used 1 cup ketchup, 1 Tbspn BBQ sauce, 1 Tsp Worchestershire sauce, 3/4 bottle of beer, 1/4 tsp of dry mustard, 2 cloves of garlic (crushed), and a dash of cayenne pepper. I also seared the pork chops with some steak seasoning and then through everything in the crock pot with 1/2 a large onion. Put on low all day then served over brown rice and peas. Super yummy and kids loved it!

Very yummy!! I will defiantly be making these again! I ended up cooking my pork chops in the crock pot (for 6 hours) instead of the oven for convenience. They turned out very tender and juicy. I followed the advise from a lot of other reviews and added a little Mustard and Worcestershire sauce. I also put in 1/2 of a onion chopped and 5 cloves of garlic minced. They were a hit! Thank you Sadie for the delicious recipe!

I was looking for a pork chop recipe that sounded yummy and was simple. This recipe was a great find! I seasoned the chops first but still let them sit in the sauce for almost and hour before baking. I highly recommend thicker cut, bone-in chops. My 3 year old devoured 2 of the pork chop bones, in addition to a decent portion of meat as well. Not sure how much of a difference it made but I used Yuengling Lager this time. I think some darker beers would be quite interesting. I also have on hand some "Taste #5 Umami Paste" so I added a few squirts of that. All things considered, they were some of the best pork chops we've had in a long, long time! Thanks!

I have a version of this recipe. It is the same but uses less beer (3/4 cup) and more ketchup. Season the chops with salt , pepper then brown in oil on both sides. Remove chops, drain out oil. Stir in sauce in skillet. Add the chops and let simmer, covered over medium to low heat. They come out so tender and with so much flavor! Doesn't taste like barbecue sauce but is very tasty! My family loves this recipe.

I seared the chops with salt (w/ out sauce) before placing them in the oven. Baked them in the oven, cut down the cooking time. Added some cayenne powder and black pepper to the sauce. It was delicious! Loved it!! definitely a keeper! Did not expect it to be soo good! Had reservations about it but seriously surprised me! Its a must. I will be keeping this recipe and using it in the future!
Amazing recipe. Since I had little time to cook, I decided to finish it in a frying pan, the whole meal got ready in 20 minutes

I do pretty much as the recipe said. I add a little garlic, pepper, and sea salt to taste. I let them sit in the sauce in a ziploc bag for about 2 hours. then I cook it at about 250 F for 15 minutes then 325 for another 10-15 so that the porkchops are nice and moist. I've also tried a little more ketchup for a thicker sauce and added a bit of soy sauce so it wasn't too sweet. My hubby and i love it.

Delicious, tender chops that whole family enjoyed. I served it with spinach, and rice that I cooked with the chops as others suggested. I made it almost exactly as written but I did brown the chops with a little garlic first. Next time I will add less sugar as it was a little sweet for my taste but that's the only change I'd make. Great easy supper!

We loved it, but I modified it for a diabetic. I used Splenda brown sugar in this recipe. Two cups of ketchup has a lot of sugars. I found a copy cat recipe for ketchup and subbed Splenda for the corn syrup and sugar to make enough ketchup. These substitutions made a very thin sauce in the baking pan after the chops were done. I put the sauce in a sauce pan on the stove top and thickened it with corn starch. I will make this again.

Hubby loved it. Very surprised he liked it as much as he did. I thought it was good but would use thicker chops than I did and about 3/4 of the beer just to make the sauce thicker.
BUT still 5 stars as I made it exactly like the recipe and it turned out great.
We loved this, it has become one of my husband's favorites. I did make a small change, I used a 1/4C mustard and 1/4C ketchup. We give it a 5 star rating!
This recipe is always a hit in our house! I use about half a beer and add a pinch more brown sugar but everyone always devours it
This is so easy and awsome. Don't need to change a thing
Great recipe!!!!!! Add some beer, garlic, ketchup and cooked for 12/hrs @ slow cooker. Everyone love it
This was horrible. Way too much ketchup!!! I won't be making this again.
I have this in the oven right now. I tried the sauce before baking and get a strong sense of the beer. I like it, but not sure my family will. I hope the beer taste will cook off some.
Really easy to make!!! Came out really tender!! Only added some garlic powder!!
